clue.text: It's fashionable to no longer think on the point of quality — that's cheap!

indicators.note: in a down-the-page sense, one piece placed on, after, the others in the charade

parts.note: IN means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
EX means former, no longer so, as in an ex-wife
pensive means thinking deeply, lost in thought
a ness is a headland or promontory, a point of land

explanation.surface: A rant that it is trendy to stop thinking about quality, which the speaker dismisses as cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the headland NESS after the rest of the charade; the definition is the quality of being cheap, read from the last words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being low in price is the property described; the noun names the condition of costing little.

clue.text: I and a friend take it in to copy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word it is taken in, placed inside the word for a friend

parts.note: a mate is a friend or pal

explanation.surface: Someone and their friend adopt a style in order to copy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take ... in' is the container signal: the friend's word swallows 'it', and the lone I stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic someone is to reproduce what they do, a straight synonym for copying.

clue.text: A pressing time

definitions.meaning: pressing clothes makes them flat and smooth, a making level
the part of the day after afternoon and before night

explanation.definitionFit: Ironing smooths fabric, an act of levelling; separately the word names the hours after dusk.

clue.text: Florence reaping worms for the bird

indicators.note: to worm is to wriggle and twist, so the letters of the two words writhe into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian woman harvesting earthworms to feed to her pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worms' is a verb here, telling you to rearrange FLORENCE and REAPING together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast hunting raptor, a large hawk-like species famous for its diving speed.

clue.text: Ed and Lionel made engraved ornamental metalwork

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned or constructed, so the two names are worked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Two craftsmen named Ed and Lionel produced some decorative engraved metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' signals rearranging ED and LIONEL. Niello is a black metallic inlay filling engraved lines in silver, so the word describes metal decorated that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black alloy inlaid in engraved silver; something treated with it is decorated with that ornamental inlay.

clue.text: There are always notes here — needs to be for good music

definitions.meaning: inside a melody is where musical notes are always found

definitions.text: needs to be for good music
definitions.meaning: an instrument or singer must be at the correct pitch for the music to sound good

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means inside a melody; idiomatically it means at the right pitch.

clue.text: Threesome forever involved with an instrument

parts.note: eternal means lasting forever
a triangle is a percussion instrument, a bent steel bar struck with a beater

explanation.surface: A trio of people bound together for life with a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a love affair involving three people, typically a couple and a lover.

clue.text: A measure of disorder when there's work in the doorway

indicators.note: the word for work sits inside the word for the doorway

parts.note: an entry is an entrance, a doorway
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone describing how messy things get when building work is being done at the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: OP for opus is a standard crossword abbreviation for a musical work; 'when there's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and information theory this quantity gauges randomness within a system.

clue.text: A false report of man's man losing his head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the word for the man is dropped

parts.note: a man from the Isle of Man is a Manxman, an islander

explanation.surface: A rumour that a masculine fellow has been beheaded, or has lost his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's man' looks like a macho type but means a man of the Isle of Man, an ISLANDER; 'losing his head' drops its first letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Defamation in spoken form is an untrue and damaging statement about someone.

clue.text: Seriously, I make a living in the home

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the words for making a living are placed inside the word for the home

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's
to earn is to make a living

explanation.surface: Someone earnestly declaring that they work from home.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a statement of fact, but 'in the home' is the container instruction, not a place of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning sincerely, not joking; an adverbial match for the clue word.

clue.text: Run more than usual

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run scored without the ball hitting the bat, such as a wide or bye

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a run not credited to the batsman (a bye, wide or no-ball) is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket run from a bye or wide carries this name; as an adjective it means additional or surplus.

clue.text: A company is maturing

parts.note: ging is an old word for a company or gang of people

explanation.surface: A firm that is growing up and becoming established.
explanation.walkthrough: GING is an obsolete word for a gang or company of people, found in larger dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing older and developing is the present participle sense; a straight synonym.

clue.text: The best sheets and what you do with them for decoration

parts.note: the finest bed sheets are made of linen
after washing, sheets are folded

explanation.surface: Fine bedding and the way you store it, presented as ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Linenfold is carved panelling in wood made to look like folded cloth, common in Tudor houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved wooden panel pattern imitating folded cloth, used as ornament in Tudor woodwork.

clue.text: For example, granny starts clockwork device in the kitchen

parts.note: EG is short for exempli gratia, meaning for example

indicators.note: the start of the word granny gives only its opening letter

parts.note: a clockwork mechanism used to count down minutes is a timer

explanation.surface: Grandma winding up a mechanical gadget in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' takes the G that opens 'granny'; the clockwork mechanism gives TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand glass or dial used for timing boiled eggs is a familiar kitchen gadget.

clue.text: For each receiving present for performer

indicators.note: the word for each takes in, receives, the word for present

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'
to lay is to present or put forward, as in lay a case before a court

explanation.surface: A gift being handed out to each entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a noun meaning gift, but it is a verb, to lay before someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor or musician is someone who takes part in a show; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Gail and Mona play about in the tree

indicators.note: playing about suggests messing around, so the letters of the two names are jumbled

explanation.surface: Two girls, Gail and Mona, frolicking up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play about' rearranges GAIL and MONA.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering tree or shrub with large showy blooms, an example of the class.

clue.text: Hollow footwear for an alien

parts.note: a sock is a piece of footwear
ET is the alien from the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A space creature being given an empty shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: ET is the extra-terrestrial from the film of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye or a plug socket is a cavity into which something fits; the noun sense of a hollow.

clue.text: Establish position of renegades travelling northwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so the words for position and renegades are taken backwards together

parts.note: to put something is to position or place it
rats are deserters or turncoats

explanation.surface: Locating where a band of deserters is heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling northwards' reverses PUT and RATS as one string, PUTRATS read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a business or system is to found it; a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Enclosure for bird's bed

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
pit is informal British slang for bed

explanation.surface: A pen with a nest bed for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT is British slang for bed; a cockpit was originally a pit for cockfighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a pit for cockfights, the word also means the pilot's compartment, an enclosed space.

clue.text: Decency of blonde's cape

parts.note: fair means light-haired, blonde
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: A golden-haired woman's cloak is a sign of her respectability.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and even-handed treatment of others is a form of propriety and honesty.

clue.text: Choose artist who loved her father

parts.note: to elect is to choose by voting
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Picking a painter whose devotion to her dad is notable.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is a standard crossword artist. In Greek myth the daughter of Agamemnon was devoted to him and avenged his murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon's daughter in Greek tragedy, whose devotion to him gave her name to a psychological complex.

clue.text: Begin showing audacity without the use of a whip

indicators.note: the beginning of the word showing gives only its first letter
the word a is not used, so its letter is taken out of the word for audacity

parts.note: courage is boldness, audacity

explanation.surface: Advice to start being bold without resorting to the lash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Begin showing' gives S; 'without the use of a' drops an A from COURAGE, leaving COURGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash used to punish, as in flogging; the noun sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Soda drink circulated round the vehicle

indicators.note: the word for drink goes around, encircling, the word for the vehicle

parts.note: to bib is an old word for drink, tipple
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink passed around a car.
explanation.walkthrough: BIB is an old verb meaning to tipple; 'circulated round' tells you it encloses the vehicle's word. Bicarb is short for bicarbonate of soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate, called baking soda, goes by this short informal name.

clue.text: Rugger ace in and around action produces a curving effect

indicators.note: the letters weave in and around one another, a signal to rearrange them

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, or rugger
A is short for ace in a deck of cards

explanation.surface: A star rugby player weaving through the play creates a bending run.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a player weaving through a move; 'in and around' is the signal to mix the letters, and 'produces' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The term means arching or bending into a bow shape, as in an arcade of arches.

clue.text: Caterpillar found in a wet oak leaf

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A grub discovered on a damp oak leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: An aweto is a New Zealand caterpillar killed and mummified by a parasitic fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Zealand moth larva infected by a fungus, prized as a carving material by the Maori.

clue.text: Question whether troops inch unevenly

indicators.note: taking the uneven, odd-numbered letters of the words picks every other one

explanation.surface: Asking whether soldiers are making slow and halting progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unevenly' takes the odd letters of TROOPS INCH: T, O, P, I, C.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion is a matter at issue; the sense of question as an issue.

clue.text: Gorilla at loggerheads with a snapper!

indicators.note: being at loggerheads means in conflict, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An ape squaring off against a creature with snapping jaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loggerheads' scrambles GORILLA and AT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A large reptile with powerful snapping jaws, a crocodilian.

clue.text: Apply war paint

parts.note: read as a Native American warrior's face being painted, it hints at a phrase for looking cheerful despite trouble

explanation.walkthrough: To 'put on' is to apply; a brave is a Native American warrior; and his face paint is literally war paint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hiding fear or distress behind a show of courage.
